scenario: A POST created a new resource
notes: Return the new resource or a link to it. Use 202 instead when the creation finishes later.

scenario: The request was accepted but will be processed later
notes: Do not promise the outcome. Give the client a status resource to poll.

scenario: The request worked and there is nothing to return
notes: Typical for DELETE and for updates that return nothing. Send no body.

scenario: A conditional GET found the client copy still valid
notes: Send no body. Repeat the validators used for the request.

scenario: A resource moved permanently to a new URL and the method must be kept
notes: Use 301 only when changing a POST into a GET is acceptable.

scenario: The resource was removed on purpose and will not come back
notes: Use 404 when you do not know or do not want to say.

scenario: The body is malformed: broken JSON, wrong types, bad query string
notes: Use 422 when the syntax is fine but the content breaks the rules.

scenario: The body is well formed but fails validation rules
notes: Return one entry per invalid field, preferably as problem details.

scenario: Credentials are missing, expired or invalid
notes: Tell the client which scheme to use.

scenario: The caller is authenticated but not allowed to do this
notes: Consider 404 when even the existence of the resource must stay hidden.

scenario: The resource does not exist, or must not be revealed
notes: Keep the body free of internal details.

scenario: The method is not supported for this resource
notes: List the supported methods in the Allow header.

scenario: A duplicate create or a state conflict, such as a version that already exists
notes: Say which state conflicts so the client can decide what to do.

scenario: A lost-update guard: If-Match does not match the current ETag
notes: Pair with 428 to make conditional writes mandatory.

scenario: The request body is larger than the server accepts
notes: State the limit in the message.

scenario: The Content-Type of the request is not supported
notes: List the accepted media types in the message.

scenario: The client exceeded its rate limit
notes: Clients should back off for the indicated time.

scenario: An unexpected failure inside the server
notes: Log the details and return a correlation id, not the stack trace.

scenario: An upstream dependency returned an invalid answer
notes: The failure is behind this server, not in the request.

scenario: The server is overloaded or in maintenance
notes: Temporary by definition; say when to retry when you know.

scenario: An upstream dependency did not answer in time
notes: Distinguish it from 503 so that operators can tell them apart.
